ai.literal: Human beings indeed they resemble, the base; like them, an exact likeness we have seen not.
ai.translation: The base perfectly resemble normal human beings. We have never seen such an exact physical likeness anywhere else.
ai.modern: கயவர்கள் பார்ப்பதற்கு நல்ல மனிதர்களைப் போலவே இருப்பார்கள். அவர்களைப் போன்ற ஒரு துல்லியமான ஒப்புமையை நாம் வேறு எங்கும் கண்டதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses biting irony to describe base or wicked people. It states that the only remarkable thing about the base is how perfectly they resemble actual human beings in their physical appearance. By saying 'we have never seen such an exact likeness', the poet implies that on the inside, they lack all human virtues and are entirely different from true humans.

ai.literal: Good than those who know, base people fortune they possess; in the heart sorrow they are without.
ai.translation: The base are more fortunate than those who know what is good, for they have no sorrow in their hearts.
ai.modern: நன்மை எது என்று அறிந்து செயல்படுபவர்களை விட கயவர்கள் பாக்கியசாலிகள்; ஏனென்றால் அவர்கள் மனதில் எந்தக் கவலையும் இருப்பதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses sharp irony to describe the nature of base people. It claims that the mean-spirited are luckier than the wise who know what is good. While good people constantly worry about doing the right thing and feel sorrow for the suffering of others, the base have no such moral anxiety. Because they lack a conscience, their hearts are completely free from distress.

ai.literal: Gods they-are-like the-base; they-too themselves desired-things having-done because-of-behaving.
ai.translation: The base are just like the gods, because they too live doing whatever they please.
ai.modern: கயவர்கள் தேவர்களைப் போன்றவர்கள்; ஏனென்றால் தேவர்களைப் போலவே கயவர்களும் தாங்கள் விரும்பியதை எல்லாம் செய்து நடப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses sharp irony to compare the lowest kind of people to the gods. It states that the base are equal to the gods because both groups do exactly whatever they desire. However, the underlying meaning is that while gods act freely due to their supreme nature, the base act freely because they lack all moral restraint. The word 'மேவன' means things that are desired, highlighting how the base are driven entirely by their own selfish whims.

ai.literal: wicked person / those who are / if seen / than them / having exceeded / will be proud / base person
ai.translation: If a base person sees someone who is wicked and unrestrained, he will outdo them in wickedness and feel proud of himself.
ai.modern: கீழான குணமுடையவர்கள் தங்களை விட மோசமானவர்களைக் கண்டால், அவர்களை விடத் தாங்கள் இன்னும் மோசமாக நடந்து கொண்டு பெருமைப்படுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the competitive nature of base people in doing wrong. When a vile person encounters someone who is wicked and unrestrained ('அகப்பட்டி'), they do not feel disgust or try to avoid them. Instead, they strive to exceed that person's wickedness ('மிகப்பட்டு') and actually take pride ('செம்மாக்கும்') in being worse. It highlights how baseness celebrates and escalates bad behavior rather than correcting it.

ai.literal: Fear indeed of the base people conduct; remainder, desire if there is, there will be a little.
ai.translation: Fear alone dictates the good conduct of the base. Otherwise, they might show a little good behavior if they desire some gain.
ai.modern: கீழானவர்களின் நல்லொழுக்கம் என்பது அச்சத்தினால் மட்டுமே ஏற்படும். அது தவிர, அவர்களுக்கு ஏதாவது ஒன்றின் மேல் ஆசை இருந்தால் மட்டுமே சிறிது நல்லொழுக்கம் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the motivations behind any good behavior seen in base individuals. The word 'ācāram' refers to proper conduct or good behavior, which in their case is driven entirely by 'accam' (fear) of punishment or authority. The word 'eccam' means remainder or exception; the only other time they might show a little good conduct is if they have an 'avā' (desire or craving) for some personal gain. Thus, their actions are never guided by inherent virtue, but only by fear or greed.

ai.literal: Beaten drum like-they base-people, themselves heard secret to-others having-carried because-of-telling.
ai.translation: Base people are like a beaten drum, because they carry the secrets they have heard and broadcast them to others.
ai.modern: கயவர்கள் தாம் கேட்ட ரகசியங்களை மற்றவர்களிடம் கொண்டு சென்று சொல்வதால், அவர்கள் அடிக்கப்படும் பறையைப் போன்றவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares base people to a drum that sounds when beaten. Just as a drum loudly broadcasts whatever strikes it, base people cannot keep a secret. When they hear something confidential, they immediately carry it to others and proclaim it. The word 'aṟaipaṟai' perfectly captures their loud, indiscriminate gossiping nature.

ai.literal: Wet hand they will not shake off base people, jaw who break bent hand-people to those who are not.
ai.translation: The base will not even shake the water off their wet hands for anyone, except to those with clenched fists who will break their jaws.
ai.modern: தங்கள் தாடையை உடைக்கும்படி முறுக்கிய கைகளை உடையவர்களுக்கு அன்றி, மற்றவர்களுக்குக் கயவர்கள் தங்கள் ஈரக்கையிலிருந்து ஒரு துளி நீரைக்கூட உதற மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet vividly illustrates the extreme stinginess and cowardice of base people. The phrase 'ஈர்ங்கை விதிரார்' (they will not shake their wet hands) means they will not even let a drop of water fall from their washed hands if it might benefit someone else. However, they will readily yield to 'கொடிறு உடைக்கும் கூன்கையர்' (those with clenched fists who break jaws). The base only give or show respect out of physical fear and violence, never out of generosity or goodwill.

ai.literal: When told, will be of use the noble; sugarcane-like, when crushed, will be of use the base.
ai.translation: The noble will be of help as soon as they are told of a need. The base, like sugarcane, will yield their benefit only when crushed.
ai.modern: சான்றோர்கள் ஒரு குறையைச் சொன்னவுடனேயே உதவி செய்வார்கள். ஆனால் கயவர்கள், கரும்பைப் போல நசுக்கிப் பிழிந்தால்தான் மற்றவர்களுக்குப் பயன்படுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts how noble and base people offer help. The word 'சொல்ல' indicates that noble people readily provide assistance the moment a need is spoken. In contrast, base people are compared to sugarcane. Just as sugarcane yields its sweet juice only when it is physically crushed ('கொல்ல'), base people will only be of use when they are forced or pressured.

ai.literal: What is worn and what is eaten, if sees upon others, fault to see capable becomes the base person.
ai.translation: If a base person sees others well-dressed and well-fed, he becomes capable only of finding faults in them.
ai.modern: பிறர் நல்ல உடைகளை உடுத்துவதையும் நல்ல உணவை உண்பதையும் கண்டால், அவர்கள் மேல் குற்றங்களை மட்டுமே காணும் இயல்புடையவன் கீழ்மகன்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the deeply envious nature of base people. When they see others enjoying good food and clothing, they cannot tolerate their prosperity. Instead of feeling happy or remaining indifferent, their immediate reaction is to search for blemishes ('வடு') in those prosperous people. The words 'உடுப்பதூஉம்' and 'உண்பதூஉம்' use elongated vowels (aḷapeṭai) to emphasize the abundance and quality of what is worn and eaten by others, which triggers the base person's jealousy.

ai.literal: For what are they fit, the base? One (trouble) when befalls, for selling are they fit, having hastened.
ai.translation: What are the base actually good for? When trouble strikes, they are only fit to quickly sell themselves.
ai.modern: கயவர்கள் எதற்குத்தான் பயன்படுவார்கள்? ஒரு சிறு துன்பம் வந்தாலும், தங்களை விரைவாக விற்றுக்கொள்ளவே அவர்கள் பயன்படுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet asks a rhetorical question: what purpose do base people serve? The word 'எற்றிற்கு' (for what) sets up this inquiry into their usefulness. The answer is that when 'ஒன்று' (one thing, implying a hardship or crisis) happens to them, they will immediately sell themselves out. 'விற்றற்கு' (for selling) means they will compromise their dignity, betray others, or literally sell themselves into servitude to escape trouble. Thus, their only predictable utility is their swift readiness to abandon their principles when pressured.
